prospective_scoring_rule: A forecast is eligible for scoring only if scored=true and its created_date is on or before its forecast publication date. Retrospective decompositions are preserved for methodological transparency but excluded from Brier scores and calibration.

protocol.calibration_policy: Report Brier scores for all resolved core forecasts and separately by event family and comparable horizon only when sample size is adequate; never imply meaningful calibration from very small cells.
protocol.change_policy: Protocol v1 is frozen for prospective use. Substantive changes require a new numbered protocol version, an effective date, a change log, and no retroactive application to already-issued forecasts.

core_scored_set.threshold_note: The 25%/30-day threshold is a monitoring convention chosen ex ante for Protocol v1 for scoreability and sensitivity to acute depreciation; it is not claimed to be a universal economic definition. Sensitivity at 20% and 30% will be reported when resolving.

core_scored_set.resolution: Corroborated settlement disruption lasting at least 14 days in at least two essential-import categories—food or grain, medicine or medical inputs, or critical energy or industrial inputs—combined with broad emergency foreign-exchange, import, or payment restrictions or a material shift by suppliers to prepayment or cash because established settlement channels are failing. Evidence must come from at least two independent source streams.

protocol.deadline_convention: Protocol v1 horizons use local-calendar time: 90-day forecasts resolve 90 local calendar days after forecast_open at the same local clock time; 12-month forecasts resolve on the same local calendar date and clock time one year later (Feb 29 maps to Feb 28). Offset may change with daylight-saving time. This convention is executable in the validator.
protocol.display_clarification: Warning colors describe the current state of a diagnostic failure pathway. Forecast probabilities describe the chance of a defined future event by a stated deadline. A severe current warning and a lower future-event probability, or vice versa, are not inherently inconsistent.
protocol.evidence_balance_policy: For each core forecast, preserve material evidence that raises, lowers, or is genuinely ambiguous/neutral. A zero probability revision may be labeled 'offsetting evidence' when meaningful opposing evidence changed but net probability did not.

evidence_impact_scale.major: High-quality evidence of a structural break, threshold crossing, major military/political/economic event, or failure/restoration of a critical mechanism.
evidence_impact_scale.minor: Credible evidence that modestly updates one input but does not alter the central mechanism or threshold state.
evidence_impact_scale.moderate: Corroborated evidence that materially changes a key driver, threshold state, or one core forecast's assessment.

evidence_reliability.High: Primary/direct evidence or multiple independent highly credible sources; direct and current; no material contradiction.
evidence_reliability.Low: Single-source, materially indirect, stale, contested, or weakly observable evidence. Low evidence cannot by itself trigger Critical.
evidence_reliability.Medium: Credible but indirect, incompletely corroborated, or subject to meaningful measurement/reporting uncertainty.
evidence_reliability.Medium-high: Credible and substantially direct evidence with at least one corroborating stream, or exceptionally strong single-source evidence.

haircut_protocol.dependence_rule: Component contributions are not simply interpreted as independent risks. Protocol v1 applies a 20% overlap deduction to the combined delivery + sanctions/payment + political-tail subtotal above 20 percentage points, rounded to the nearest point, to reduce double counting of a common geopolitical shock.
haircut_protocol.overlap_status: The 20% overlap factor is an explicit Protocol v1 convention, not an empirically estimated correlation parameter. It is a candidate for empirical revision only in a future protocol version.
haircut_protocol.sensitivity: Alongside the v1 20% overlap convention, report sensitivity using 0%, 20%, and 40% overlap deductions. The 20% case remains the Protocol v1 headline; sensitivity cases are diagnostic and do not change the frozen rule.

houthi_protocol.elicitation: Assess matériel and technical/financial support separately from local capability; headline probability is a judgment conditioned on at least one Iranian-support channel remaining strategically meaningful.

id_policy.evidence_id: Persistent event/source identifier. Reuse the same evidence_id when evidence is carried forward; mark evidence_status='new' or 'carried_forward' rather than creating a duplicate observation.
id_policy.forecast_id: core event id + '_' + forecast date YYYYMMDD; immutable once issued.

protocol.noncore_policy: Other probabilities may be published as diagnostic estimates but are not part of the permanent core scored set unless added prospectively in a later protocol version.
protocol.publication_architecture: Current Pages source is main. Protocol v1 publication procedure validates the proposed record before commit and CI validates again after push. A future candidate-branch/merge gate is preferred for stronger pre-main atomicity; until implemented, a failed CI run must not be represented as validated.

resolution_policy.authority: Resolve from the pre-specified event rule using the archived public evidence record. Ambiguous cases require a written resolution note citing the decisive evidence and rule clause.
resolution_policy.indeterminate: If reliable public evidence is insufficient to determine Yes or No by the resolution review date, code outcome='indeterminate'. Indeterminate forecasts are excluded from Brier/calibration scoring; the exclusion and reason remain public. Never choose a resolution based on which result improves the score.
resolution_policy.review_timing: Perform resolution review promptly after the forecast deadline; later evidence may establish what happened before the deadline only if it directly documents the pre-deadline state.

protocol.revision_attribution_rule: At forecast time, record approximate signed percentage-point contributions for material new evidence/reassessment sufficient to reconcile the prior point forecast to the new point forecast. These are an audit decomposition of judgment, not causal estimates or a statistical model. If effects offset, label offsetting evidence.
protocol.serial_dependence_caveat: Weekly forecasts with overlapping horizons are strongly serially dependent. Per-forecast Brier scores may be reported, but counts of overlapping forecasts must not be interpreted as independent sample size; calibration uncertainty and comparative claims must account for clustering/overlap.
protocol.timestamp_policy: Evidence collection closes before forecast elicitation. Each update records evidence_cutoff as the actual last evidence timestamp used and publication_time as the actual commit/publication timestamp. Material information first available after evidence_cutoff is excluded from that forecast and may enter only the next forecast or an explicitly labeled interim update.
protocol.uncertainty_display: Display the reasonable-analyst interval less prominently than the point forecast and evidence confidence until external forecaster dispersion can be compared with it.

uncertainty_rule.definition: The displayed judgmental uncertainty range is the interval within which the assessor judges that roughly 80% of independent, well-informed analysts using the same public information, event definition and horizon would place their point probability. It measures model/analyst disagreement, not sampling error, a Bayesian credible interval, or the probability that the true probability lies in the interval.
uncertainty_rule.elicitation: Set the point forecast first. Then estimate the 10th and 90th percentiles of the distribution of reasonable analysts' point forecasts without changing the point forecast to center the range.
uncertainty_rule.name: Reasonable-analyst interval

protocol.validation_policy: Errors block validation: malformed core records, wrong deadlines/timestamp ordering, post-cutoff evidence with known publication time, arithmetic failures, or unauthorized historical mutation. Missing precise source publication time is a validation warning and must remain explicitly recorded as unknown.

method.label: Model estimate
method.rule: Central haircut = sum of six bounded component haircuts: physical delivery/blockade 0–25 pp; sanctions/payment channels 0–15; sovereign/counterparty 0–10; oil-price/basis 0–8; illiquidity/enforcement 0–8; political/secondary-sanctions tail 0–8. Each component is assigned from documented weekly evidence using Low/Mid/High anchors at 25/50/75% of its cap; the central estimate is the sum rounded to the nearest percentage point. The judgmental range is formed by moving each uncertain component one anchor step down/up, bounded at zero/cap. This is not an observed contract price.

houthi.definition: Strategically meaningful Houthi support is decomposed into Iranian matériel flow, Iranian technical/financial assistance, and Houthi independent/local capability.
